question.problem:
Consider a system of two linear equations in two variables, represented by the matrix equation $Ax=b$ in the usual way. Given that the system has exactly one solution, which of the following statements are true?

I. $det(A)\ne 0$

II. $A$ is  invertible

III. $Ax=0$ has a nonzero solution
question.worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

1\. $A$ is invertible.

2\. The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

3\. The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

4\. The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

5\. $det(A)\ne 0.$

Also, we are told that the second part of the invertible matrix theorem is true. So, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement I is true by the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement II is true by the first part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement III is false by the third part of the invertible matrix theorem.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
